newsitem.title: USA: Starbucks offers reward on triple homicide.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks offers reward on triple homicide.

text.p: Starbucks Corp. on Tuesday offered a $50,000 reward to find the killer of three young employees slain in one of their fashionable coffee shops in Washington's upmarket Georgetown area on Monday.

The Seattle-based national coffee chain also established a memorial fund in memory of the two men aged 18 and 25 and 24-year-old woman killed in the unusual slaying in a relatively safe part of the wealthy neighborhood.
The fund was for the victims' families or their designated charities.
The company said it would hold a memorial service for all company employees at a date and location to be determined soon.
All three of the victims were found with at least one gunshot wound to the head shortly after 5:15 a.m. EDT Monday by a colleague arriving for work.

The coffee shop remained closed Tuesday as police continued their investigation into the triple homicide. A company spokesman said Starbucks would decide when, and if, to reopen the store once the investigation was completed.

Police had no further comment on the case, but local television reported that at least one former Starbucks employee had been interviewed, although he had been all but ruled out as a possible suspect.
The victims were Aaron David Goodrich, 18; Mary Caitrin Mahoney, 24; and Emory Allen Evans, 25, all of whom lived in Washington.
